source_record_title: USPS Mail Consolidations and Trump EO Create Ballot Delivery Crisis Before 2026 Midterms
split_rationale: The supplied record combines a USPS postmark clarification and a distinct presidential executive order. Sources support two separately dated developments, but do not support a single nationwide ballot-delivery crisis or the claimed causal connection between USPS operations and ballot rejection counts.

children.title: USPS Clarifies How Machine Postmarks Record Postal Possession
children.description_short: USPS clarified that processing-facility postmarks may be later than first postal possession; the revision did not change existing postmarking practices.
children.description_medium: The Postal Service’s postmark revision, effective December 24, 2025, explained that a processing-facility postmark reflects the first automated processing date, which may follow initial postal possession. USPS said the text did not change existing operations and described manual counter postmarks that can match the mailing date. It did not establish late-ballot counts or ballot-rejection effects.
children.description_long: USPS’s Domestic Mail Manual revision concerning postmarks and postal possession took effect on December 24, 2025. The Postal Bulletin says the added section defined qualifying postmarks, described when they are applied, and explained how customers can obtain evidence of the date USPS accepted mail. It expressly says the wording did not change existing postal operations or postmarking practices. Under the stated standard, an automated processing-facility postmark shows the date of the first automated processing operation; that date may be later than the date USPS first took possession. USPS separately said transportation adjustments meant some mailpieces might not reach their originating processing facility on the day they were mailed. A customer presenting mail at a retail counter could request a manual local postmark aligning with the date of acceptance, and USPS said the guidance also applied to mail-in ballots. These sources support a description of the clarification and disclosed operating context. They do not establish a count of late ballots, a particular election’s rejection total, or that the rule caused a voter’s ballot to arrive late. The materials also do not attribute this USPS action to Trump. This child records that bounded postal development without repeating the combined card’s unsupported claim of a nationwide ballot-delivery crisis.

source_fact_map.fact: The Domestic Mail Manual standards became effective December 24, 2025.
USPS described the new DMM language as a clarification that did not change existing operations or postmarking practices.
source_fact_map.quote: This new language in the DMM does not change any existing postal operations or postmarking practices
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: This new language in the DMM does not change any existing postal operations or postmarking practices but is instead intended to improve public understanding of postmarks and their relationship to the date of mailing.

source_fact_map.fact: A processing-facility postmark date may be later than USPS first accepted the mailpiece.
source_fact_map.quote: the postmark date does not necessarily indicate the first day that the Postal Service had possession of the mailpiece
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: The presence of a postmark confirms that the Postal Service accepted custody of a mailpiece, and that the mailpiece was in the possession of the Postal Service on the identified date. However, the postmark date does not necessarily indicate the first day that the Postal Service had possession of the mailpiece.

source_fact_map.fact: USPS said transportation adjustments could mean some pieces did not reach originating processing facilities on the day mailed.
source_fact_map.quote: adjustments to our transportation operations that will result in some mailpieces not arriving at our originating processing facilities on the same day that they are mailed
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: While we are not changing our postmarking practices, we have made adjustments to our transportation operations that will result in some mailpieces not arriving at our originating processing facilities on the same day that they are mailed.

source_fact_map.fact: USPS said the same guidance applied to mail-in ballots.
source_fact_map.quote: This guidance is the same for all types of mailpieces, including mail-in ballots.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: As before, a customer can ensure that a postmark is applied to his or her mailpiece, and that the date on the postmark matches the date of mailing, by visiting a Postal Service retail location and requesting a manual (local) postmark at the retail counter when tendering their mailpiece. Manual postmarks will be applied free of charge. This guidance is the same for all types of mailpieces, including mail-in ballots.

children.title: Trump Signs EO 14399 Directing USPS to Propose Mail-Ballot Standards
children.description_short: Trump’s March 2026 election order directed USPS to propose ballot-mail standards; it did not itself enact a ballot-refusal rule.
children.description_medium: Trump signed EO 14399 on March 31, 2026, directing USPS to propose mail-in ballot service standards and DHS to compile state citizenship lists. It called for proposed envelope markings and barcodes; it did not itself enact ballot-refusal rules. California DOJ reported key provisions remained blocked in plaintiff states during appeal.
children.description_long: On March 31, 2026, President Donald Trump issued Executive Order 14399, titled “Ensuring Citizenship Verification and Integrity in Federal Elections.” Among other directions, the order told the Postmaster General to start a proposed rulemaking within 60 days for USPS mail-in and absentee ballot services. The notice was to include proposed requirements such as an Official Election Mail marking and a unique Intelligent Mail barcode on outbound ballot mail. The same order directed the Department of Homeland Security, with Social Security Administration coordination, to compile and transmit state citizenship lists to chief election officials. These passages show a signed executive order directing a rulemaking process; they do not show that USPS had already adopted a rule refusing to carry ballots based on a federal voter list. In July 2026, California’s Attorney General reported that the First Circuit left a district court order blocking key provisions in place for the plaintiff States while the appeal proceeded, including the USPS ballot restriction and DHS eligibility lists. That is a party’s public account of the court posture, scoped to those states and that period. No fact in the source packet establishes that the order caused a nationwide ballot-delivery crisis, the stored California rejection count, or the alleged local advice to abandon mail voting. This child therefore describes the enacted order and proposed USPS action separately from implementation, litigation, and broader effects.
children.subcategory: Federal election administration and ballot mail

source_fact_map.fact: The White House identifies EO 14399 as dated March 31, 2026.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt:
# ENSURING CITIZENSHIP VERIFICATION AND INTEGRITY IN FEDERAL ELECTIONS

March 31, 2026

Executive Order 14399

source_fact_map.fact: The order directed the Postmaster General to initiate a proposed rulemaking for USPS ballot-mail services.
source_fact_map.quote: the Postmaster General is hereby directed to initiate a proposed rulemaking
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: To protect the integrity of the mail as a medium for transmitting Federal election ballots and establish uniform standards for mail-in or absentee ballot services implemented through the United States Postal Service (USPS), the Postmaster General is hereby directed to initiate a proposed rulemaking pursuant to 39 U.S.C. 401 and other applicable authority within 60 days of the date of this order.

source_fact_map.fact: The proposed notice was to include Official Election Mail markings and a unique Intelligent Mail barcode for outbound ballot mail.
source_fact_map.quote: Proposed provisions specifying that all outbound ballot mail must be mailed in an envelope
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: The notice of proposed rulemaking shall include, at minimum, the following: Proposed provisions specifying that all outbound ballot mail must be mailed in an envelope that is marked as Official Election Mail and is automation-compatible and bears a unique Intelligent Mail barcode.

source_fact_map.fact: The order directed DHS, coordinating with SSA, to compile and transmit state citizenship lists to state election officials.
source_fact_map.quote: shall take appropriate action to compile and transmit to the chief election official of each State a list
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: The Secretary of Homeland Security, through the Director of United States Citizenship and Immigration Services and in coordination with the Commissioner of SSA, shall take appropriate action to compile and transmit to the chief election official of each State a list of individuals confirmed to be United States citizens who will be above the age of 18 at the time of an upcoming Federal election and who maintain a residence in the subject State (State Citizenship List).

source_fact_map.fact: California DOJ reported that the First Circuit denied a stay request and left key provisions blocked in plaintiff States while the appeal proceeded.
source_fact_map.quote: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit denied requests by the U.S. Department of Justice and intervenor states to pause a district court order blocking key provisions of the Executive Order in the plaintiff States
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit denied requests by the U.S. Department of Justice and intervenor states to pause a district court order blocking key provisions of the Executive Order in the plaintiff States for the upcoming fall midterm elections while the appeal proceeds. Specifically, the district court’s order blocks a provision that directs the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) to issue regulations that would prohibit the mailing of ballots to voters who are not included on new USPS lists of “enrolled” mail voters.
